inspection_summary: Inspected all 1337 frozen logical lines (1314 LF-delimited physical lines plus 23 form-feed page boundaries). The extraction is unusually strong for prose and most formulas. The source nevertheless has a strict evidence hierarchy: Lemmas 1-2 are proved in the paper; Theorems 1-2 are conditional on explicit conjectures; the factor-of-two diffusion claim and critical-dimension law include heuristic steps; figures and fitted exponents are numerical evidence; and the RH/GRH links are formal contour arguments with an acknowledged unproved contour-closing condition. A few multi-factor displays, especially the Epstein factorization and Dirichlet-character expression, need PDF verification before exact transcription.

sections_inspected.label: Title and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Announces multidimensional infinite-horizon diffusion, conditional formulas, numerical simulations, a proposed critical dimension, and an RH connection.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reviews proved two-dimensional finite/infinite-horizon limit laws and defines the higher-dimensional scope and order of limits.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Diffusion coefficients
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates moment-defined diffusivity from limiting-law covariance in logarithmic superdiffusion and proposes a rare-flight explanation for their discrepancy.

sections_inspected.label: Figure 2 and 3. Summary of results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces horizon taxonomy, states three conjectures and two conditional theorems, and explicitly qualifies the formal RH connection.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Definitions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines phase space, free-flight survival, horizons, maximal/principal/incipient status, and the infinite lower-dimensional structure attached to incipient horizons.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Two lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves finiteness of maximal horizons, explains why a two-dimensional proposition fails to generalize, and proves each non-incipient horizon's survival asymptotic.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Principal horizons and the free flight function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Enumerates horizons by primitive dual-lattice vectors, derives the survival lattice sum, tests it numerically, and uses Mellin inversion to formulate a conditional RH/GRH-sensitive small-scatterer expansion.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Incipient horizons and the critical dimension
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives a limiting cusp geometry and horizon-sum convergence threshold, then uses simulations to support a conjectured change of decay at dimension six.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Correlations and diffusion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tests the decorrelation conjecture numerically, proves the conditional superdiffusion theorem, and transfers the formal RH remainder to diffusivity.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Diffusion in discrete time
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates continuous-time covariance to collision-time covariance through the mean free time and gives the resulting horizon formula.

accepted_units.title: Finite and infinite horizon produce different proved scaling laws in two dimensions
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes established results: bounded free paths yield Brownian scaling proportional to t, whereas infinite corridors retain Gaussian limits with the nonstandard t log t scale. It also separates discrete-time proofs from continuous-time convergence and fixes the order of the small-scatterer and long-time limits used later.
accepted_units.context_note: These are literature-backed results summarized by the author, not new proofs in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose-supported; exact normalization is stated clearly enough, though displayed square roots should be checked before quotation.

accepted_units.title: Macroscopic diffusivity, microscopic moments, and Gaussian covariance
accepted_units.why_material: The diffusion PDE, its Gaussian Green function, and the displacement second moment establish the conventional relation between diffusivity matrix D and limiting covariance Sigma=2D. The unit fixes factors and distinguishes moment convergence from weak convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both macroscopic and microscopic descriptions because the later anomaly is meaningful only relative to this baseline.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: formulas (1)-(6) are legible; exact matrix indices and square-root scaling should be PDF-checked for formal reuse.

accepted_units.title: Weak convergence need not determine anomalous second moments
accepted_units.why_material: For logarithmic superdiffusion the source defines a moment coefficient D and a limiting-law covariance Xi separately, then explains why slowly spreading tails can make weak convergence compatible with nonconvergent or differently normalized moments. It also contrasts continuous-time slow correlations with discrete-time infinite single-flight variance.
accepted_units.context_note: Statements about future higher-moment proofs at lines 141-145 are proposals attributed to other work, not established here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the distinction is prose-clear; formula (7) has extraction ambiguity in the square-root normalization and should be checked exactly.

accepted_units.title: Finite-time Gaussian cores coexist with ballistic expanding tails
accepted_units.why_material: Figure 1 numerically shows convergence of the scaled core toward a normal law while lattice oscillations and collision-free ballistic spikes remain in expanding tails. This is source evidence for the mechanism by which moments can exceed the covariance seen in the weak limit.
accepted_units.context_note: This is simulation evidence at r=0.4 and selected times, not a proof of the asymptotic moment relation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: figure labels and caption preserve the qualitative observation; numerical curve values are not tabulated.

accepted_units.title: Rare free flights predict a factor-two separation between moment and limit-law coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Exact corridor formulas from the literature are reconciled by a heuristic tail cutoff: collision-free probability decays only like 1/t, so the converged Gaussian core captures half of the logarithmic second moment. The author therefore proposes Xi=D rather than the normal-diffusion relation Xi=2D.
accepted_units.context_note: Equations (9)-(11) cite established coefficient formulas; equations (12)-(13) and the half-contribution argument are explicitly heuristic; the final arbitrary-dimensional extension is a proposal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: coefficient formulas are readable, but the tail-balance normalization and lower-order terms should be verified before quantitative use.

accepted_units.title: Horizon dimension and collision-free survival organize long flights
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces a binary finite/infinite classification with sets of collision-free phase points carrying a velocity subspace dimension. It defines horizon-specific survival FH(t) and distinguishes maximal, principal, and incipient horizons, predicting which dimensions can contribute to leading survival and superdiffusion.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a summary-level framework; full definitions are supplied later in u13-u14.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: formula (14) and geometric notation are legible.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 1: non-incipient maximal horizons dominate survival
accepted_units.why_material: The conjecture asserts that the leading free-flight probability is the finite sum of maximal non-incipient horizon contributions, treating incipient horizons, lower-dimensional horizons, and overlaps as subleading. The source explicitly identifies this as a geometric, not dynamical, unproved step.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite-sum fact is later proved separately; dominance itself remains conjectural.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: statement and qualifications are prose- and formula-clear.

accepted_units.title: Conditional survival asymptotic as a sum of visibility integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 combines Conjecture 1 with two later lemmas to express the leading free-flight probability through horizon dimension, lattice covolume, and a visibility-counting double integral. It converts global survival into finite local geometric contributions.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is proved only conditional on Conjecture 1; its proof here is a dependency reduction to Lemmas 1-2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (16) is multi-line and should be checked against the PDF before exact transcription, although its factors are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 2: incipient horizons create a critical dimension at six
accepted_units.why_material: Heuristic summation and later simulations motivate t^-2 decay below dimension six, an additional logarithm at six, and an unknown fractional exponent between one and two above six.
accepted_units.context_note: Every branch is conjectural; the logarithm at d=6 is described as tentative, and the exponents above six are not derived.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the piecewise display (17) is readable semantically but its exact asymptotic symbol and layout need PDF confirmation.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 3: colliding trajectories decorrelate below the free-flight scale
accepted_units.why_material: A grazing-collision scaling argument motivates that correlations from trajectories with at least one collision are little-o of the collision-free survival probability. This isolates uninterrupted flights as the leading correlation mechanism needed for diffusion.
accepted_units.context_note: The square-root post-collision flight estimate is heuristic and the integral bound is an explicit conjecture, with stated model limitations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: conjecture formula is legible.

accepted_units.title: Principal horizons determine the superdiffusion matrix and link it to survival
accepted_units.why_material: Conditional on Conjectures 1 and 3, Theorem 2 sums projected horizon directions weighted by squared widths to obtain D. Taking the trace and combining with Theorem 1 yields the geometry-independent relation dD=lim tF(t), while incomplete spanning predicts degenerate superdiffusion.
accepted_units.context_note: Both the matrix and trace relation inherit all conjectural dependencies; the full conditional proof occurs in u27.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (18) is multi-line but recoverable; exact normalization should be PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: The initial RH connection is explicitly formal rather than an equivalence proof
accepted_units.why_material: The author explains that small scatterers generate increasing lattice-horizon sums whose Mellin transforms contain inverse zeta factors. The proposed RH link requires contour closure along pole-avoiding semicircles, and the source explicitly says that a complete equivalence proof is unavailable even for a simpler analogue.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit prevents the paper's title and later asymptotic from being misread as a proved RH criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the proof gap and analogy are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Phase space, collision time, and survival sets
accepted_units.why_material: The compact quotient phase space, invariant probability measure, billiard flow, next-collision time, and survivor set Mt make the free-flight function F(t) an exact measure-theoretic object. Zero-measure collision ambiguities are separated from the asymptotic problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the formal base for all horizon and correlation statements.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: definitions (20 onward are outside this span); the measure normalization and set notation are clear.

accepted_units.title: Horizons arise from rational velocity subspaces and connected spatial components
accepted_units.why_material: Free torus trajectories either become dense or lie parallel to lattice-spanned subspaces. The source uses this dichotomy to construct velocity sets, quotient the spatial direction, and define an inextensible horizon with connected spatial projection; examples show why one direction can support multiple horizons.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes equations (20)-(25), Definition 1, and induced perpendicular lattice geometry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: direct-sum, quotient, and covolume notation are dense but recoverable; exact superscripts should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Incipient horizons contain infinitely many lower-dimensional horizon directions
accepted_units.why_material: Maximal and principal horizons are dimension-based, while an incipient horizon has zero transverse measure. In dimensions above two, shrinking a higher-dimensional horizon creates a lattice of tangencies and countably many subordinate horizon directions, explaining why naive finite dominance fails at the transition.
accepted_units.context_note: Definitions 2-5 and the geometric mechanism are source statements; claims about complexity are analogical rather than a derived asymptotic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-medium: prose and definitions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Only finitely many maximal horizons exist
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 proves finiteness by showing that infinitely many connected components conflict with finitely many convex scatterer pieces, while infinitely many increasingly dense velocity subspaces force a larger horizon and contradict maximality.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an actual proof in the source, not conditional on Conjecture 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: proof is prose-geometric.

accepted_units.title: A two-dimensional corridor covering proposition fails in higher dimensions
accepted_units.why_material: Long paths in higher dimensions can traverse a complicated connected network of horizons of different dimensions, so Bleher's bounded-exception corridor proposition cannot be reused. Intersections, non-maximal horizons, and infinitely many subhorizons in the incipient case are exactly the omissions delegated to Conjecture 1.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a method-comparison and obstruction unit, not a proof of the conjectured dominance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: A single horizon contributes a visibility-weighted power law
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 decomposes position and velocity into parallel and perpendicular components, rescales transverse velocities by 1/t, and integrates the visible transverse region to prove FH(t) decays as t^{-(d-dH)} with an explicit geometric coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: This lemma is proved unconditionally for a non-incipient horizon; using its sum as F(t) still needs Conjecture 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (26) and visibility integral are recoverable but should be checked exactly before symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: Primitive dual vectors enumerate principal horizons with a width cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: Codimension-one horizon lattices correspond to primitive dual-lattice vectors modulo sign. For spherical scatterers the horizon exists exactly below a length cutoff and has width L^-1-2r; inserting these widths into conditional Theorem 1 yields the explicit finite lattice sum for F(t).
accepted_units.context_note: The lattice correspondence and geometry are argued directly; equation (27) inherits Conjecture 1 through Theorem 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: dual-lattice normalization, inversion factor, and equation (27) require exact notation preservation.

accepted_units.title: Dimension-wide simulations test the horizon-sum survival laws
accepted_units.why_material: The source describes collision computation, boundary-accuracy safeguards, and precision checks, then compares dimensions 2-10. Results support C/t for principal horizons and qualitatively support C/t^2 for overlapping-scatterer lower-dimensional horizons, with explicitly worsening statistics and convergence at high dimension.
accepted_units.context_note: This is numerical corroboration, not a proof of Conjecture 1 or of the uncomputed C/t^2 coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose, captions, and axes support qualitative conclusions; raw simulation data are not included.

accepted_units.title: Mobius inversion and Mellin transform expose inverse-zeta poles
accepted_units.why_material: Mobius inversion removes the primitive-vector constraint, and a Mellin transform converts the cutoff lattice sum into a contour integral containing an Epstein zeta numerator and 1/zeta(s+1). Residue expansion would translate poles into small-r powers.
accepted_units.context_note: The identities are presented formally; the author explicitly cannot prove a sequence of left-closing contours whose integrals vanish.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: equations (28)-(30), contour placement, and arguments of both zeta functions must be PDF-checked before exact use.

accepted_units.title: RH controls the proposed small-scatterer remainder, conditional on contour closure
accepted_units.why_material: Known analytic properties of Epstein zeta locate the numerator's pole and zeros, while zeros of zeta(s+1) create denominator poles. Under the unproved contour step, the leading Boltzmann-Grad term has an O(r^{1/2-delta}) remainder for every positive delta if RH holds; numerical residue sums support the smooth real-pole terms, and the source only suggests an equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: Epstein continuation/factorizations are cited facts; equation (31) and any RH equivalence remain conditional. Figure 5 is numerical evidence, not validation of the missing contour argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the Z4 factorization at lines 857-863 has damaged exponents, and equation (31)'s exact coefficient/remainder should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Rational multi-scatterer cells introduce Dirichlet characters and a GRH analogy
accepted_units.why_material: For rationally located multiple scatterers, the Mellin calculation is said to replace the scalar sums by Dirichlet L-functions and twisted Epstein zeta functions, creating a formal route from transport to generalized RH.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a sketched extension, not a proved GRH equivalence; the three-dimensional twisted Epstein factor is explicitly difficult to characterize.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: equation (32) is layout-damaged and cannot be transcribed reliably without the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Incipient-horizon rescaling produces an L^-5 contribution and critical summability threshold
accepted_units.why_material: At touching radius, each incipient coordinate plane contains horizons indexed by all primitive lattice vectors. Rescaling the two-dimensional transverse gap yields a universal four-parabola region; its visibility integral is numerically estimated and gives FH(t) proportional to t^-2 L^-5. Summing indices becomes an Epstein series convergent through dimension five and divergent from six.
accepted_units.context_note: The rescaling and series convergence criterion are analytic; the visibility constant 0.02746 is numerical, and divergence alone does not determine the new time exponent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: limiting shape (33), order of limits, and formula (34) are readable but formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Fitted survival exponents support a change near dimension six
accepted_units.why_material: Figure 7 and Table 2 compare dimensions 2-10 at touching radius. Low dimensions approach exponent two, while dimensions six and above show smaller fitted exponents, qualitatively supporting Conjecture 2 while revealing strong finite-time drift.
accepted_units.context_note: The author emphasizes low packing fraction, slow convergence, unknown high-dimensional exponents, and finite-time exponents above two in lower dimensions; these fits are not asymptotic proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: table values and caption are legible.

accepted_units.title: Velocity correlations are compared directly with free-flight predictions
accepted_units.why_material: The source tests Conjecture 3 by fitting velocity autocorrelation to C_r/t and comparing C_r with the horizon-sum limit of tF(t) across scatterer radii. This is the empirical bridge from collision-free geometry to diffusion.
accepted_units.context_note: Figures 8-9 provide numerical comparison only; the later text says accessible diffusion times are dominated by normal contributions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-medium: captions preserve the intended comparison, but underlying sample sizes and uncertainties are not tabulated.

accepted_units.title: Proof of Theorem 2 reduces correlations to constant-velocity horizon integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming Conjecture 3 removes colliding trajectories at leading order and Conjecture 1 replaces survivors by maximal horizons. Repeating the transverse scaling of Lemma 2 and integrating vv over the horizon sphere gives the projection matrix and completes Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: The integral evaluation is proved, but dominance of collision-free and maximal-horizon terms remains conjectural.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (35)-(36) and normalization need exact checking.

accepted_units.title: Explicit cubic diffusivity inherits the same formal RH remainder
accepted_units.why_material: For ranges with specified horizon families the conditional theorem yields explicit isotropic diffusivity. In the fixed-d, small-r limit the survival relation transfers equation (31)'s RH-sensitive remainder directly to D.
accepted_units.context_note: Formula (37) inherits Conjectures 1 and 3; formula (38) additionally inherits the unproved Mellin contour step. The claimed RH equivalence is again only an appearance under that caveat.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: threshold radii and coefficients in (37)-(38) should be PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: Mean free time transfers continuous covariance to collision-time covariance
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes the formally infinite discrete moment coefficient from the finite covariance of the limiting law, uses the mean free time to relate discrete and continuous covariance, and derives a simplified horizon sum for the discrete-time covariance.
accepted_units.context_note: The transfer uses the earlier proposed Xi=D relation and conditional Theorem 2; mean-free-time formulas are cited/derived for non-overlapping scatterers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (39)-(41) are readable but exact surface-measure normalization should be checked.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Limit-law covariance and second moments probe different parts of a heavy-tailed distribution
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Gaussian core determines weak convergence while rare ballistic flights dominate an additional half of the logarithmic second moment, motivating Xi=D rather than Xi=2D.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The core/tail observation is numerical and the exact half-contribution is heuristic, not proved by the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Horizon codimension controls survival decay and only principal horizons yield logarithmic superdiffusion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A single horizon contributes t^{-(d-dH)}; conjectural dominance by maximal horizons and decorrelation of colliding trajectories then makes codimension-one horizons the unique source of 1/t correlations and logarithmic superdiffusion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The single-horizon exponent is proved, while global dominance and correlation reduction are Conjectures 1 and 3.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Mobius inversion turns primitive geometric counting into an RH-sensitive analytic remainder
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Removing primitivity introduces an inverse Riemann-zeta factor; Mellin residues then make the small-scatterer error exponent sensitive to zeta zeros and transfer the same formal remainder from survival to diffusion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The contour-closing sequence is unproved, so neither the expansion nor its suggested equivalence to RH is established.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: An incipient horizon changes a finite dominant family into a summability problem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At the touching transition, countably many subordinate horizons contribute with L^-5 weights; their lattice sum changes from convergent to divergent at dimension six, providing a mechanism for a critical decay law.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Divergence proves neither the logarithm at d=6 nor the fractional exponents above it; those remain conjectural and numerically supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The paper's evidence chain must remain typed
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Proved local lemmas feed conditional global theorems; independent simulations test selected consequences; RH and critical-dimension claims add further analytic or heuristic assumptions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Agreement of figures with predictions cannot promote conjectures or formal contour arguments to proofs.

stop_reason: All 1337 logical lines were inspected. The accepted units cover every distinct mathematical mechanism, theorem, conjecture, obstruction, numerical test, and RH-sensitive argument. Remaining lines are historical/application context, figure scaffolding already attached to evidence units, acknowledgements, references, or routine repetition; further splitting would duplicate mechanisms rather than add source-supported meaning.
